questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Califorina to try what the American college experience is like. With campus located right on the beach, and almost all students living side-by-side, Santa Barabra was a great option. I also wanted to explore national parks and have great nature experiences and California is great for this.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It is fun but it is also tough.
six months was enough for me i wouldn't want to stay for a full year.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Housing was difficult, but it seems like it worked out for everyone.
Introductionto the campus and the system was very nice and easy by the help of OISS.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: i got a campus tour and an internationals meeting about how the campus worked.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I went with an option listed by the university as an alternative to campus housing that way it seemed legit. a lot of other stuff looked shady.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It seemed more fun than to live on campus in this instance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Im not used to sharing a room and paying over 1000 bucks a month to do so is straight up insane. But that is how it is in Isla Vista at the moment.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most things are possible if you ask.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You log into the website called UCSB GOLD. Here you can find courses for next quarter and add them to your basket if you find them interesting you can also start to plan you schedule here. You get three pass times. In the first pass time you can select up to 8 units which is approx. two courses within your major. For each passtime more courses opens up from other faculties and you can fill in more units. You can add or drop courses on the first week of class without penalty and if a course is full you can "crash" in the first week and talk to the instructor who can ive out add codes. It is a good strategy to add more classes than you expect to take and try it out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The advisors at the different faculties. On email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of them. Soemtimes they took place at the same time and that is just unfortunate.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write emails if you want soemthing. it is almost always possible to get in somehow. and crash courses in the beginning but make up your mind fast, because the instructors chooses the people thay have seen participate.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it varies from faculty to faculty. Within STEM the material was on a high level and the students were dedicated. Outside not so much. The teaching varies very much with the instructor. It is very different from home.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took upper division BA-classes which is what corresponds to second and third year on UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is way more homework than expected. There is fewer sections wit a TA. It seems like youhave to perform and hand in all of your work which i think is a challenge in actually learning the material. The exams are very diferent. Closed book, closed notes. More like learn by heart and rememeber.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Philosophy of space and time
Intermediate python programming
California physics

Planets and exoplanets
Softmatter physics
Geography of surfing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Planets and exoplanets was fun because it had a different approach then what im used to in physics. There as a final project about rewriting a scietific article to a popular scientific article. That was fun.
Prof. Wang in the python class is one of the best instructors I've seen.

Food was way more.
Beer was a little more.
ialmost didn't buy books because the taches didn't follow/use them and published nice notes or I could get them at the library.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Surfing was great

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there were a lot of clubs and nice facilities for physical activity.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the Excursion club they do fun trips and it is a nice way to meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Roadtrip is a classic. You can get far.
Go to channel islands.
Surf at devs.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty straight forward sometimes you would get some cultural surprises but mostly it is also what we came for.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Tag along with housemates when they go out and do something and host some parties.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I mostly found the food and eating habits different and at times challenging. I just expected it to be more like home.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Being invited to something by complete strangers. They are very open to new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
No need to do more than 12 units even thouh it is possible.
Buy a wetsuit and borrow surfboards from excursion club (their wetsuits are very old)
Find a group of international friends that also wanna go around Califrnia in the weekends and split the cost of renting a car.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't buy the UC health insurance search up ISO and get the same for half the price.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The American friends i now know who will come visit me here and i can visit in the future.
An understanding of how americans think and live.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my partner at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
